chapter: Russell and Armstrong years, Goodman and the road
title: Lucky Millinder as bandleader
summary: Millinder played no instrument but was a smart director; Joe Garland and George Washington arranged.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What instrument did Lucky Millinder play?
He didn't play no certain instrument.
He was just one of the best directors and produced.
And how! A really smart man. He could make them up just like this, and couldn't read a note.
But you say he never played drums or piano or anything. He just stood in front and conducted a band?

He had rehearsals, maybe a week or so ahead of time he would think of a tune. When he would get it together in his head then he would call a rehearsal and Joe Garland made the arrangements, a tenor sax player. He would hum off the tunes and Joe Garland would copy them down and make the arrangement.
Who else made arrangements in the band.
George Washington, trombone player. Let's see, who else? I think that's all.
